51847.body:
### PR description:

(Re-)Built on top of #52015 and validated also on top of #52011.

As of today, it is meant to be used at HLT in Phase-2 and it requires an update to the corresponding JSON: https://github.com/cms-data/RecoTracker-MkFit/pull/21, which goes on top of https://github.com/cms-data/RecoTracker-MkFit/pull/22.

Its two goals, removing more duplicates and recovering efficiency in dense jets, are addressed by a new cleaner, `phase2:clean_duplicates_sharedhits_pixelpriority_ptadaptive`.

#### What the new cleaner does
It applies #52015's pixel-priority rules, plus:

1. **Low-pT shared-hit fraction.**
   - When the harder track of a pair is below 5 GeV, the shared-hit fraction is lowered to 0.10, 
   and interpolated back up linearly in 1/pT back to its "default" value at 10 GeV.
2. **The low fraction applies only to pairs consistent with one particle:**
   - relative 1/pT difference at most 0.1;
   - same charge;
   - both tracks with |d0| to the beam spot below 2 cm;
   - R(, ) below 0.1 GeV / pT of the harder track.
3. **Unique-hit keep rule.**
   - A track with pT  10 GeV that would be removed is kept if it has at least 9 found hits not shared with the other track.
4. **Direction tests in  and in  at the beam spot.**
   - The cleaner uses  instead of cot  in its direction tests: the broad window applied to every pair, and the direction-only test.
   - It uses  at the point of closest approach to the beam spot instead of the momentum .
5. **Only pairs sharing a hit are compared.**
   - With the direction-only test off, two tracks can only be duplicates if they share a hit.
   - The cleaner therefore takes the candidate pairs from a hit  tracks index instead of looping over all pairs.

#### Implementation and configuration
- **Code structure:** the cleaner is a second template flag on #52015's implementation, relying on its pixel-priority keep rule and distinct-pixel-seed guard. `phase2:clean_duplicates_sharedhits_pixelpriority` and `phase1:clean_duplicates_sharedhits_pixelseed` are unchanged.
- **Parameters:** they are `MkFitIterationConfigESProducer` parameters (`duplicateCleaningLowPtFraction`, `LowPtRampStart`, `LowPtRampEnd`, `LowPtMaxRelDiffInvPt`, `LowPtRequireSameCharge`, `LowPtMaxD0`, `LowPtMaxDRTimesPt`, `MinUniqueHitsToKeep`, `MinPtUniqueHitsToKeep`).
  - Their defaults are listed explicitly in `hltESPMkFit_cfi.py`.
  - They are ignored by the other cleaners.
- **Phase-2 region boundaries:** the region boundaries of the direction-only test are the Phase-2 tracker ones, now expressed in  (|| = 1.0 and 2.4). With the current phase-2 HLT mkFit JSON configuration, that test is switched off (`dc_drth_* = 0`).
- **Interface change:** duplicate cleaners now also receive the beam spot. `runFunctions.cc` and the standalone drivers are updated.
- **Selection:** the cleaner is chosen by `m_duplicate_cleaner_name` in `RecoTracker/MkFit/data/mkfit-phase2-lstStep.json`, which cms-data/RecoTracker-MkFit#21 changes. Until that change is in, the LST step keeps running #52015's cleaner.

#### Validation
Validated with the MultiTrackValidator on `hltGeneralTracks`, relative to #52011 + #52015, on 5000 events each of tt and QCD (pT 1.82.4 TeV), both with PU200 and compared on the same events.

- **Overall:** the duplicate rate drops from ~1.25% to ~0.95% in tt  and in QCD. The fake rate also slightly decreases. The overall efficiency is ~ unchanged in tt  and in QCD.
- **Below 10 GeV:** the fake plus duplicate rate drops by about 15% (duplicates 20-25%, fakes 2 to 3%; 30% duplicates for || > 3), with prompt efficiency unchanged within 0.01 percentage points.
- **High-pT jets:** in QCD, efficiency rises from 71.5% to 74% above 100 GeV and slightly at 10100 GeV. The cost is a 1015% relative increase of the fake plus duplicate rate above 10 GeV.
- **Displaced tracks:** efficiency changes by 0.05 and 0.01% at production radii of 1030 and 30100 cm in tt, and increases by 0.2 and 0.1% in QCD. The same holds for in-time pileup tracks, checked at truth level.
- **Timing:** the new cleaner is about 60% faster than #52015's, saving about 3 ms per event (about 1.5% of the HLT tracking time).

**MTV plots**:
- #52011 + #52015 vs this PR:
  - tt: https://uaf-10.t2.ucsd.edu/~mmasciov/MIC/Phase2/PR51847/hltMTV_TTbar_PU200/plots_hlt.html
  - QCD: https://uaf-10.t2.ucsd.edu/~mmasciov/MIC/Phase2/PR51847/hltMTV_QCD_Pt1800to2400_PU200/plots_hlt.html
51847.title: Introduce mkFit pT-adaptive pixel-priority duplicate cleaning for phase-2

51864.body:
This pull request add two services to be used in conjunction with Vtune profiling.

The first VtuneAnnontateService marks the modules listed in the configuration with a string for highlighting it in the Vtune gui. This service can be run multithreaded.

The second VtuneFilterService pauses Vtune profiling when the modules selected in the configuration are running. Since the methods `__itt_pause()` and `__itt_resume()` pause and resume profiling for all threads in the process, the process should be run single threaded.

For finer grained pausing, the suggested method is to create a `__itt_scoped_pause` object in the function to be filtered out. This requires `#include ittnotify.h` and adding `<use name="ittnotify"/>` to `BuildFile.xml`. The object calls `__itt_pause()` on creation and calls `__itt_resume()` upon destruction when the function goes out of scope. The implementation uses environment variables defined while running Vtune to enable the calls. This means that there is no overhead in adding this object to the function to be skipped.


Produces this warning when `__itt_pause()` is first called
```

vtune: Collection paused.
```

#### PR description:

Phase-2 Outer and Inner Tracker modules and sensors need to be masked out of reconstruction and simulation to study detector failure scenarios. There is currently no dedicated mechanism to do this for the Phase-2 tracker. This PR is the first step: it adds the payload infrastructure to mask hand-specified bad sensors for both the Outer and Inner Tracker, reusing the existing Phase-1 `SiPixelQuality` CondFormat payload. Currently one has to specify the sensor DetID's one wants to disable in a .txt file, one file per subsystem.

The design was reworked during code review: it originally supported a combined module/sensor-list input shared across both subsystems with silent cross-subsystem filtering; it now uses one flat sensor-DetId list per subsystem, with a hard failure on any subsystem mismatch.

This PR consists of three commits:

1. **Adding EventSetup records for Phase-2 bad-sensor payloads.** New `SiPhase2InnerTrackerBadSensorRcd`/`SiPhase2OuterTrackerBadSensorRcd` (`CondFormats/DataRecord`).
2. **Registering Phase-2 bad-sensor records with `SiPixelQuality` in the CondDB plugin**. Couples both new records to the existing `SiPixelQuality` payload type (`CondCore/SiPhase2TrackerPlugins`).
3. **Adding hand-specified Phase-2 bad-sensor builder and reader, with tests**. `SiPhase2BadSensorsByHandBuilder` reads one flat text list of sensor DetIds per job instance (`badSensorListFile`), one instance per subsystem (OT or IT); to disable a whole module, both of its sensor DetIds are listed explicitly. `SiPhase2BadSensorsByHandReader` reads the payload back and logs each disabled DetId (collapsing module pairs into one line when both sensors are present), as a verification tool.

The example DetId list files used by commit 3's test configs live in `cms-data/CondTools-SiPhase2Tracker` repo. A separate PR for that is made over in that repo.

At later stages, other possibilities to populate the DB will be added (like via ESSource). Digitizer extension to accept this payload is also in the works.

52171.body: #### PR description This PR was co-developed by the NGT Task 3.1.1 team: @rovere, @mmusich, @JanGerritSchulz, @elenavernazza, @bfonta, @EmanueleCoradin together with inputs from @borzari and @AdrianoDee. Some of the developments were assisted by AI tools, including Claude (Sonnet / Opus / Fable) and Kimi K3. Wherever possible, we have tried to preserve co-authorship of commits, including both human and AI authors. In this PR we introduce a new heterogeneous collection of Outer-Tracker `VectorHits`, built on device following the existing fully serial `VectorHit` formalism. Additionally, the PixelTracking CA is re-envisioned and extended to take full advantage of hits from the Pixel detector and the aforementioned `VectorHits` in the OT. This is the first implementing PR for Iterative Tracking on Accelerators with Cellular Automaton (ITACA), further improvements to the fit and physics reach are expected to follow. Preliminary results for the full chain were shown at the [24/08 TRK POG meeting](https://indico.cern.ch/event/1719987/#1-update-on-extension-of-ca-an). Edit: the PR has since been shown at the 27/10 RECO meeting ([link](https://indico.cern.ch/event/1744784/#7-extension-of-ca-and-usage-of)) and in more details with comparison plots and a full overview of the new models (with re-training instructions) at the 02/11 TRK POG meeting ([link](https://indico.cern.ch/event/1747859/#11-status-update-on-vectorhits)) ##### Main developments - New `reco::VectorHitsSoA` / `reco::OTRecHitsSoA` collections (`DataFormats/TrackingRecHitSoA`) with ROOT dictionaries. The CA reads pixel hits and vector hits through a single bounds-checked interface (`CAHitsView`), implemented with the same API as the existing SoAMultiView to maintain easy backwards compatibility via type aliasing - The vector hits implementation is bundled together with its validation via a new DQM module (+ harvesting) - OT RecHit conversion for the CA (`hltCAOTRecHitsSoA`), run-dependent stacked-module geometry (`StackedModuleGeometryESProducer`), and vector hits formation kernels (`Phase2OTVectorHitsSoAProducer`) - The cellular automaton is extended to the full tracker, with pixelvector hit and vector hitvector hit doublets, vector-hit-curvature-based triplet criteria, and an optional in-kernel triplet/track DNN (compile-time weight banks, off by default to not change physics, but enabled for the VectorHit configuration) - To better integrate these developments into the full tracking chain at HLT, the `removeOTRechits` flag found in the `SeedGeneratorFromProtoTracksEDProducer` (`hltInitialStepSeeds`) has been modified to feed the same seeds for both the default (extended) PixelTracks and the vector-hit based ones. In particular, the flag is now turned on by default with no change in the behaviour for the default chain, since it keeps all hits from the IT and P hits from OT PS modules in the barrel - The CA kernels and fit orchestration are now split per topology (`Phase1` / `HIonPhase1` / `Phase2` / `Phase2OT` / `Phase2OTVectorHits`) to reduce single-TU compile times - The CA can now optionally rely on two in-kernel DNNs (with weights saved as constants in header files) to select High-Purity triplets (`useTripletDNN`) and assign tight quality to tracks (`useTrackDNN`). Again, these flags are only turned on for the new vector-hit-based CA. Furthermore, for this updated configuration, the final HP selection has replaced the torch DNN with a compact gradient-boosted forest - Another new CA flag, `useExactAllocations`, was introduced to allow to further reduce the memory footprint on GPU by computing the exact number of doublets before allocating their container. This leads to another potential memory saving, but comes at the cost of one event synchronisation, whose impact on timing strongly depends on how full the GPU queue is. The flag is disabled by default, since the trade-off is not currently worth it and memory reduction has been achieved in other key areas by cost-free developments - A lot of developments have gone into reducing the memory footprint of the entire CA chain. While most benefits are observed when using vector hits, the default configuration also benefits from some improvements that specifically targeted the heaviest consumers of memory (doublets, triplets, tracks) - Some other miscellaneous improvements include `OneToManyAssoc` zeroing using a device memset and `bulkFill` gaining a content-capacity overflow guard #### PR validation - Running `scram b runtests` locally shows no failures - `runTheMatrix.py -l limited -i all --ibeos` runs fine locally - Physics performance has been validated on a few samples (TTbar, high pT QCD and Z' M6000), showing PixelTracks efficiency on par or slightly better with respect to the current baseline, with much improved resolutions and reduced fake rate: [Efficiency vs eta](https://lferragi.web.cern.ch/plots/tracking_phase2/itaca/CAVectorHits/MTV/CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-10-04-0000/TTbar/hltPhase2Pixel_hltAssociatorByHits/effic.png) | [Efficiency vs pT](https://lferragi.web.cern.ch/plots/tracking_phase2/itaca/CAVectorHits/MTV/CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-10-04-0000/TTbar/hltPhase2Pixel_hltAssociatorByHits/efficPt.png) :-------------------------:|:-------------------------: | [Fake rate vs eta](https://lferragi.web.cern.ch/plots/tracking_phase2/itaca/CAVectorHits/MTV/CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-10-04-0000/TTbar/hltPhase2Pixel_hltAssociatorByHits/fakerate.png) | [pT resolution](https://lferragi.web.cern.ch/plots/tracking_phase2/itaca/CAVectorHits/MTV/CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-10-04-0000/TTbar/hltPhase2Pixel_hltAssociatorByHits/ptres_vs_eta_Sigma.png) | All plots are available [here](https://lferragi.web.cern.ch/plots/tracking_phase2/itaca/CAVectorHits/MTV/) (originally produced with `CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-10-04-0000`, updated with `CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-10-16-1000`) **Note** A new workflow such as `37834.7512` can be used to test this part of the new ITACA prompt iteration on TTBar 200 PU. The old "PixelTriplets" workflows (offsets .406-.408) have been replaced with the new ITACA prompt iteration equivalents (validation and profiling) This PR also changes the default behaviour of the `ngtScouting` procModifier, replacing the extended PixelTracks with ITACA prompt iteration **Review note** A significant number of new files and added lines come from the new compiled-in DNNs and the scripts to easily retrain them and the new forest (or existing HP DNN)

52217.author: fwyzard
52217.body: #### PR description: The streamer output modules accept `compression_algorithm` "LZ4", with `compression_level` 1 for the fast LZ4 compressor, 2 for the "mid" compressor introduced in LZ4 v1.10.0, and 3-12 for LZ4 HC. ROOT currently does not use levels 2 and 3 (but see root-project/root#23748) and stops at level 9. Compressed events start with the `L4` header, and the input sources and `DiagStreamerFile` detect and decompress them like the other algorithms. The output tests now take a compression level; NewStreamer run the round trip at levels 1 (fast), 2 ("mid") and 4 (HC). LZ4 is faster than zstd level 1, but creates significantly larger files. LZ4HC is as slow as zlib and zstd, so it's only useful when the fastest decompression is needed. #### PR validation: Unit tests pass. 52344.author: felicepantaleo
52344.body:
#### PR description:

This PR fixes three small items in the truth-graph packages.

- `truth::isShowerObject` now follows the PDG numbering scheme. It adds the gluon code 9, the generator pseudoparticle range 81-100, the reggeon 110 and the odderon 9990. `isParton` accepts 9. Before this change a reggeon counted as a hadron with an observable momentum.
- The GenEvent node now takes every GEN vertex with no incoming particle, and every GEN vertex that those vertices do not reach along the directed edges. Before this change, a component with a source vertex attached only its sources, so a beam-fed branch in the same component was unreachable. `truth::genEventAttachedVertices` holds the rule, and `TruthGraphProducer` and `TruthGraphAccumulator` both use it. For a collider record and for a particle gun, the attached vertices do not change.
- `AllRecoToTruthBranchAssociatorsProducer` takes the constituent association map type from the `ConstituentType` of the domain trait, not from a hard-coded `reco::Track`. The type does not change for the vertex domain.

- Generator-internal states in the 99xxxxx range (e.g. Pythia diffractive) are shower objects. The left-right symmetric states 9900012/14/16, 9900023, 9900024, 9900041 and 9900042 are physical particles. Their decays get the reason `Decay`, not `Hadronization`. Measured on 4 Pythia8 W_R to e N events: the 8 W_R and N vertices change from `Hadronization` to `Decay`, and nothing else changes. On 10 ttbar events no particle has a 99xxxxx code, so the result is identical.
- The truth-branch validation puts the alternative gluon code 9 in the gluon flavour bin.

#### PR validation:

- New unit tests: `LevelFlags_t::testShowerObjectsFollowThePdgScheme` and `GenGraphBuild_t::testGenEventReachesEveryVertex`. Both fail without the fix. All 14 unit tests of PhysicsTools/TruthInfo pass.
- The reference ttbar GEN record (20 events, 34981 particles) has 0 particles with the codes that change.
- `TruthGraphProducer` and `TruthLogicalGraphProducer` on 5 ttbar events: the raw graph, the logical graph and the JSON dumps are byte-identical to the baseline. The GenEvent node points to every GEN vertex in every event.
- Workflow 34834.88 (TTbar D122, no pileup) on 10 events from the same GEN-SIM, with single-stream DIGI per leg. The logical graph and the hit index in step2 are byte-identical to the baseline. In the TruthInfo DQM, 637 of 41915 monitor elements differ, with a maximum relative difference of 1.0e-6. Two baseline runs give 641 differing elements and 9.8e-7, so the change is within the noise.

52345.author: felicepantaleo
52345.body:
#### PR description:

A truth level is a full record of what it names, so `hardProcess` keeps the neutrinos of the hard scatter. No reco object can find a neutrino. A neutrino in the efficiency denominator therefore caps the efficiency below 1. On no-PU ttbar the `generalTracks` efficiency against `hardProcess` is 0.908, and the 11 neutrinos in the denominator cause all of the loss.

This PR keeps every level as it is, and `levelFlags` do not change. `TruthBranchTargetsProducer` now drops the invisible members from the level denominators `truthToRecoTargets<Level>` and from their eligibility masks. The candidate roots, `denominatorRoots` and `assignableRoots` do not change, so the association products do not change.

`PhysicsTools/TruthInfo/interface/TruthLevels.h` holds the species in one helper, `truth::isInvisible`: the neutrinos (12, 14, 16), the graviton (39), the PDG dark matter states (51, 52, 53), the lightest neutralino (1000022), the gravitino (1000039) and the Kaluza-Klein graviton (5100039). This is a subset of the CMS invisible lists in `GenSpecificAlgo.cc` and `genMetTrue_cff.py`. `truth::isInvisibleParticle` applies the list to a particle and keeps a member that the graph decays, for example a long-lived neutralino, because its decay products are visible. `truth::isNeutrino` is new. The reconstructable final state walk uses it, so the walk drops the neutrinos only, as before. `Branch::visibleP4` now excludes every invisible species.

The rule applies to every hit-based level denominator. On no-PU ttbar, `hardProcess` and `stableDecayProducts` hold neutrinos. `stableLegsFromInitialState` and `underlyingEvent` hold them when a preset builds these levels. The signal seed denominators do not change.

- `truth::isInvisibleParticle` is true when the species is invisible and every leaf below the particle is an invisible species. A copy chain of a neutrino is invisible. A neutralino that decays to visible particles is not.
- `truth::isInvisible` also holds the sneutrinos (1000012, 1000014, 1000016).
- `signalSeeds` drops invisible seeds, so a neutrino gun has an empty `signal` folder. `signalSeedsNoSelection` has no cut and keeps them. No sample in this PR books the signal folders, so this part is checked by reading only.
52345.title: Drop invisible members from the truth level efficiency denominators

52348.author: felicepantaleo
52348.body:
This PR adds the parameter `requireHits` to `TruthBranchTrackValidator`, `TruthBranchTracksterValidator` and `TruthBranchPFClusterValidator`. When it is true, a truth-to-reco denominator member is counted only when its subgraph has a hit in the detectors of the validated collection: the `denominatorDetectors` of the domain's associator (Tracker for tracks, HGCAL for tracksters, Ecal and Hcal for the PF clusters). The default is false, so the default output does not change.

- One list, `truthBranchDenominatorDetectors` in `truthGraphAssociationLabels_cff`, feeds the associators and the validators. `BranchHitAssociator::detectorMask` parses it for both, so the two cannot differ.
- The `signalNoSelection` denominator is exempt: it has no cut at all.
- `Validation/TruthInfo/customiseTruthBranchRequireHits` turns `requireHits` on for every hit-based validator of the process.
- The cut is in the validator and not in `TruthBranchTargetsProducer`, because one target list serves every domain and only the validator knows its detectors.

52358.author: GNiendorf
52358.body:
#### PR description:

This PR speeds up T5 building, the stage that dominates LST in dense events, without changing physics.

A T5 is an inner T3 (MD0-MD1-MD2) and an outer T3 (MD2-MD3-MD4), whose segments are the outer LS1 (MD2-MD3) and the outer LS2 (MD3-MD4). The first dBeta cut depends only on the inner T3 and the outer LS1, the second only on the inner T3's first segment and the outer LS2; then come the remaining cuts (radii, chi2, DNN).

Before, the T5 stage was:
- `CountTripletConnections`: one block per inner module; for every (inner T3, outer T3) pair both dBeta cuts, loosened (the full selection in dense modules); counts per inner T3 and per MD, and dBeta pass bits for the first 32 outer T3s.
- `CreateEligibleModulesListForQuintuplets` (single block): per-module T5 capacity and offsets, and the T5-by-MD ranges in a loop over the MDs of every module.
- `CreateQuintuplets`: every pair again, the full selection on each candidate, the T5 stored in a build-time collection.
- `CompactModuleOffsetsKernel`, `FinalizeQuintuplets` (fits and embedding, written at the exact size), `SetCompactModuleIndices`, after a second host synchronization.

The problems: the full selection runs a second time per candidate; the first dBeta cut is evaluated per outer T3 although it depends only on the outer LS1; a dense module of a jet core is processed by a single block, while in sparse events most threads of a block have no pair to test; the single-block kernel loops over all MDs.

After:
- `FillLSonT3ByMD` (new): per MD, the segments starting there that carry triplets (the "LS on T3"): the outer LS1 candidates of the inner T3s ending at that MD, with no loop over outer T3s.
- `CountTripletConnections` (rewritten): tiles of 64 inner T3s, one block per tile. One thread per (inner T3, outer LS1) applies the outer LS1 cuts once; then one thread per candidate (inner T3, outer T3) applies the outer LS2 cuts, through a cache of the last decision per outer LS2, and the remaining cuts. Work spreads evenly over the threads whatever the density, with the same code on every backend. Each selected pair is counted per module and per MD and recorded in a pair list; if the list overflows, the kernel is re-run with a larger one.
- `CreateEligibleModulesListForQuintuplets`: per-module counts only.
- `SetQuintupletRangesByMD` (new): the T5-by-MD ranges, one thread per MD.
- `AddSelectedQuintuplets` (new, replaces `CreateQuintuplets` and `FinalizeQuintuplets`): writes the T5s directly from the pair list at their exact size, without re-running any cut or compacting. It is launched twice (pairs of dense modules first) to keep the previous T5 order in the modules that reach the T5 cap.
- Unchanged: `ExtendT5FromDupT5ByMD`, `RemoveDupQuintupletsAfterBuild`.

All buffers that change are transient (T5 stage only); the stored T5 collection is unchanged.

#### PR validation:

HLT timing, hltLST, ms per event; Phase-2 HLT menus on CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-10-27-2300, 1 thread, median of 2 rounds:

| | master | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| CPU menu, QCD (high-pT jets) | 3150 | 1020 |
| CPU menu, ttbar | 300 | 289 |
| GPU menu (NVIDIA L40), QCD | 497 | 87 |
| GPU menu (NVIDIA L40), ttbar | 3.02 | 2.61 |

Physics: MTV, HLT and offline, 500 ttbar + 500 QCD PU200 events: efficiency, fake and duplicate rates unchanged. Plots: HLT [ttbar](https://gniendorf.github.io/lst-plots/internal-prs/lst-t5-enumeration/hlt_ttbar/plots_hlt.html), [QCD](https://gniendorf.github.io/lst-plots/internal-prs/lst-t5-enumeration/hlt_qcd/plots_hlt.html); offline [ttbar](https://gniendorf.github.io/lst-plots/internal-prs/lst-t5-enumeration/off01_ttbar/index.html), [QCD](https://gniendorf.github.io/lst-plots/internal-prs/lst-t5-enumeration/off01_qcd/index.html)

52368.body:
#### PR description:

**This PR contains the BTV DQM clean-up.** Most of the clean-up concerns the jet kinematics, so it is grouped here
with the other jet-kinematics changes:
- the duplicated per-discriminator copies of the jet kinematics are replaced by one set per tagger (item 3);
- the unused `jetMomentum` and `jetMultiplicity` histograms are removed (item 3);
- the double-filled UParT ALL histograms are fixed (item 1).

In total, about 1240 histograms removed (about 830 fewer) per workflow and the `Btag/` folder about half its size. Only the
DQM/validation code (DQMOffline/RecoB, Validation/RecoB) is touched.

1. **Fix double-filled UParT ALL histograms.** The UParT validation module used MClevel 4, which books the ALL histograms that the DQM module already books in the same folder, so every UParT ALL histogram was filled twice.
   The all-jet tag rate `jet{Eta,Phi}_diffEff_*ALL` read ~0.007 instead of ~0.3. UParT validation now uses MClevel 3 (keeps the d/u/s/g split); `jetFlavour_*ALL` is always booked.
2. **Tag efficiency vs jet pT per flavour (`jetPt_diffEff`)**, next to the existing vs-eta/phi plots. Booked for the MiniAOD taggers (UParT, ParticleNet Forward). New `FlavourHistograms::divideRebinned()`.
3. **Tagger jet kinematics once per tagger; drop jetMomentum and jetMultiplicity.** Every discriminator of a MiniAOD tagger filled the same jets, so the jet kinematics were bin-identical in all 18 UParT discriminator folders.
They now go to one folder per tagger and eta region, booked by one discriminator (UParT BvsAll, PNet Forward QvsG). New parameters `kinematicsTag` / `bookKinematics`; `bTagMiniDQM_cff.py` checks that exactly one discriminator per tagger books them. `jetMomentum` (no information beyond pT and eta) and `jetMultiplicity` (one entry per event) have no consumer in the release and are removed (MiniAOD taggers and AOD JP).
4. **Jet pT up to 7 TeV (`jetPt_extended`).** `jetPt` ([0, 350] GeV, 1 GeV bins) has up to 46 % of QCD jets (78 % of light jets) in the overflow. It is kept unchanged for the low-pT region, and `jetPt_extended` is added next to it: 700 x 10 GeV on [0, 7000] (similar to JME). The new `jetPt_diffEff` (140 x 50 GeV on [0, 7000]) is divided by `jetPt_extended`.
5. **Fill the absolute jet flavour.** `jetFlavour` was filled with the signed flavour on [-0.5, 21.5]: up to 51 % underflow (antiquarks).

Folder changes for RelMon (MiniAOD taggers):
- The jet kinematics `jetPt/jetEta/jetPhi/jetFlavour` move out of the discriminator folders `Btag/UParT_<discr>_<region>` and `Btag/ParticleNetForward_QvsG_<region>` into `Btag/UParT_<region>` (`UParT_GLOBAL`, `UParT_ETA_0-1v4`, `UParT_ETA_1v4-2v5`) and `Btag/ParticleNetForward_ETA_2v5-5`. The content is the same as the former BvsAll / QvsG copy.
- `jetMomentum_*` and `jetMultiplicity_*` are removed everywhere, including AOD `Btag/JP_*`.
- Per workflow: 1239 (Run 3) / 1233 (Phase-2) histograms removed, 408 / 405 added (kinematics in the new folders
  incl. `jetPt_extended`, `jetPt_diffEff`, `jetFlavour_*ALL`).
- UParT ALL histograms have half the entries; the plain histograms keep the same mean and RMS.

#### PR validation:

`scram b` without warnings. 
runTheMatrix steps 3+4 of workflows 16834.0 (Run 3 2025) and 29634.0 (Phase-2 D110), 100 events, compared with plain master: all steps exit 0. 
The removed and added histograms are exactly the ones listed above. The moved jetPt/jetEta/jetPhi are bin-identical to the former copies (UParT ALL: half, item 1).
Data: T0 PromptReco config (`RunPromptReco.py`, ppEra_Run3_2024, BTagMu Run2024I RAW, 1000 events), which runs `BTagPerformanceAnalyzerOnData`:
- exit 0, no BTV errors;
- 101 histograms removed (kinematics copies, jetMomentum/jetMultiplicity incl. JP), 38 added (incl. `jetPt_extended`).

52372.body:
#### PR description:

Duplicate of 17_0_X backport PR https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/52352, targeting instead master (20_1_X).

This PR updates the Phase-2 Global Trigger Emulator step-1 menu to use the latest online-to-offline scalings from [L1T annual review 2026](https://indico.cern.ch/event/1709561/), derived with the [standalone menu tools](https://github.com/cms-l1-dpg/Phase2-L1MenuTools) AR26 configs using CMSSW_17_0_0_pre6 (identical to pre7 in terms of L1 objects in the menu). 

It also adds three new menus as options for the P2GT step, e.g. `-s L1P2GT:v0p0_2026`, containing the seeds already available to be run in P2GT. The default stays `step1_2024`:
- `step1p5_2026`: the new core menu based on the Run 3 menu
- `v0p0_2026`: step 1.5 plus the available step 2 seeds and the extended-eta seeds, which will become the new baseline going forwards
- `step1and2_2026`: `step1_2024` plus the available step 2 seeds that weren't yet in the emulator, i.e the previous baseline

Seeds not-yet implementable in P2GT include the L1 Calo Tau seeds, the L1 Track-Triplet W->3pi seed, the b-tag L1 NG JetSC4 seed, and the two wide-jet L1 JetSC8 seeds that use the mass variable. The standalone L1EG seeds (both normal and extended) still use the stand-in of TkPhotons without applying isolation, but the two are equivalent physically and just differ in where the inputs come from (CL2 vs GCT).

In addition to the new menus, this updates the collection and format used in P2GT for the wide-jet objects (which hadn't previously been used in P2GT seeds) in line with the latest developments, and the thresholds in the triple TkMuon step 1 seed have been corrected (4/2 GeV to 3.5/2.5 GeV, to match the name and implementation in standalone tools). 

#### PR validation:  

In preparation: running the standard Phase-2 tests for the default `step1_2024` menu, and a comparison of standalone tools vs P2GT rates for each of the four menus: `step1_2024`, `step1and2_2026`, `step1p5_2026` and `v0p0_2026`

The test checked only the dumper structure, because its docstring said that the cff failed on import. The cff imports without error in this release, with and without `ticl_barrel`.

testPyTICLValidation compares the type, `linkingPSet` and InputTags of the supercluster module of the HLT target with the module of the HLT_75e33 menu, and checks that the HLT validation labels contain it. The second check needs #52321, which puts `hltTiclTracksterLinksSuperclusteringDNNUnseeded` in `hltTiclIterLabelsPSet`.

52380.author: felicepantaleo
52380.body:
This PR fixes five user-interface defects of the truth validation. An adversarial review found them, and each one was checked in the code. Each fix is one commit.

**The HLT PF cluster associators.** `hltTruthBranchPFClusterEcalAssociators` reads `hltParticleFlowRecHitECAL`, which no module produces, and `hltParticleFlowClusterECAL`, which the HLT output does not keep. So `customiseTruthHltValidation` and `customiseTruthGraphAssociators` stop with `ProductNotFound` on a `.88` step3 file. The ECAL associator now reads `hltParticleFlowRecHitECALUnseeded`. The customises schedule it only in a job that runs the HLT menu. `customiseTruthGraphAssociators` keeps the products of both HLT PF cluster associators.

**The order of a preset and the validation customise.** A preset reaches only the modules that exist when it runs. A validator loaded after the preset keeps the default seeds, with no error. The validation customises now raise when a preset ran before them. Apply the preset last, with `--customise_commands`, as the documentation says. A job that applies them in the wrong order now stops.

**Fragment names.** `WplusH`, `WminusH` and triboson fragments resolved to the `full` preset, with no signal. They now resolve to `vh` and `diboson`.

**The first working point.** The validators read the map of the first working point as the complete map, and only `Fixed` keeps every candidate. `TruthBranchRecoValidator` now throws when the first working point is not `Fixed`. All shipped configurations list `Fixed` first.

**`makeTruthValidationPlots.py`.**
- The script stops when two inputs hold the same folder. Before, the later file replaced the earlier one with no error.
- An empty bin no longer draws a ratio of 0.
- A negative ratio stays on the axis.
- A NaN fit no longer corrupts the y axis.
- A working point with no drawable bin no longer reads as -100%.
- The plot jobs use the cores that the job may run on, not every core of the host.

#### PR validation:

- Base: `CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-11-02-1100`.
- 3 TTbar D122 events from a step2 file through RAW2DIGI,RECO,RECOSIM: `customiseTruthGraphAssociators` and `customiseTruthHltValidation` each run, with the HCAL map and without the ECAL map.
- 3 TTbar D122 events from GEN-SIM through HLT and `VALIDATION:@hltValidation` in one job, with `customiseTruthHltValidation`: both maps run on all events. This check does not read the map contents.
- The script writes 1941 plots on a harvested DQM file of 10 TTbar D122 events.
- The runtests of the four truth packages pass. New tests cover the preset order and the fragment names. No test covers the first-working-point check or the plot script.

This PR fixes three defects in the truth graph and its analysis layer. An adversarial review found them, and each one was checked in the code. Each fix is one commit.

**Hitless pruning.**
- The upward removal deleted a decayed GEN parent that has a hit of its own, while the hit index keeps that hit. It now keeps such a parent. The new test fails without the fix.
- `dropHitlessSimSubgraphs` left the graph unpruned, with no error, when the hit vector did not align with the graph. It now throws.

**Reconstructable walk.** A `reconstructablePdgIds` entry stopped the walk for one charge only. It now stops the walk for both charges, so the list needs only one sign of each species. The two copies of the `partonJets` definition in `TruthLevels.h` become one helper.

**`truth::Branch`.**
- `finalState()` counted a root together with its own secondary when both were roots of the branch. It now starts from the earliest roots.
- A `Predicate` closure with no predicate and an `UntilPdgId` closure with no pdgId now throw. Before, they gave a full subtree.
- `merged()` across two graphs now throws. Before, it dropped the other branch with no error.

#### PR validation:

- Base: `CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-11-02-1100`.
- Sample: TTbar D122, no pileup, 10 events, single-stream DIGI, runTheMatrix `.88` recipe.

52399.body:
This PR is a follow-up to #50627.

Implement a new kind of alpaka `stream::EDProducer` that combines the non blocking synchronisation of `stream::SynchronizingEDProducer` with the fixed association of device queues to framework streams of `stream::FixedQueueEDProducer`.

This is useful for modules that need to copy data back to the host before using external software that associates resources to the device queues, for example the PyTorch device memory caching allocator. Without it, the module has to be split in two, a `stream::SynchronizingEDProducer` and a `stream::FixedQueueEDProducer`, passing the data between them as an event product.

The example use case we are working on is the TICL trackster inference on GPU, which needs the number of selected tracksters on the host to allocate the inputs of its PyTorch models.

52415.author: felicepantaleo
52415.body:
`device::Event::getHandle(device::EDGetToken<T>)` does not compile for the asynchronous backends (CUDA, ROCm). It is a template, so the error shows only when a module calls it, and no module calls it today. There are two errors in the branch for a device product held in `edm::DeviceProduct<T>`:
- the failure path passes `whyFailedFactory()`, a const reference to a `std::shared_ptr`, to the `edm::Handle<T>` constructor, which takes an rvalue reference;
- the call `getSynchronized(*metadata_)` does not give the metadata type, so the template argument cannot be deduced. `get()` in the same file calls `template getSynchronized<EDMetadata>(*metadata_)`.

This PR copies the `shared_ptr` into the `Handle` and calls `getSynchronized` as `get()` does. `TestAlpakaGlobalProducerE` now also reads its input with `getHandle()` and checks that it gives the same product as `get()`, so the device branch of `getHandle()` is compiled and run for every backend that the AlpakaTest tests use.

The TICL device reconstruction needs `getHandle()` to read the `ProductID` of a device trackster collection: the order of several trackster collections is fixed by an `edm::RefProdVector` in the event, and the consumers check their inputs against it.

#### PR validation:

Built in `CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-11-05-2300` for the serial, CUDA and ROCm backends. Before the fix, a call of `getHandle()` with a device token failed to compile for CUDA and ROCm. `HeterogeneousCore/AlpakaTest/test/testAlpakaModules.sh cpu` and `testAlpakaModules.sh cuda` pass (Tesla T4).

52426.body:
### Current setup

The Phase-2 GMT computes a **track-based** isolation for each `l1t::TrackerMuon`: `Isolation::isolation_allmu_alltrk` sums the pT of the L1 tracker tracks inside a cone around the muon and stores the result twice,

* `hwIsoSum_`  the unsaturated accumulator, LSB `LSBpt = 0.03125` GeV,
* `hwIsoSumAp_`  the same sum through `ap_ufixed<9, 9, AP_TRN, AP_SAT>` and then `>> 3`, i.e. the 6-bit word (`BITSGTISO = 6`, LSB `LSBGTiso = 0.25` GeV) that is handed to the GT.

`L1GTProducer::produceGMTTkMuons` picks up the second one via `TrackerMuon::apIso()` and fills both `hwIsolationPT_` and `isolationPT_` on the `P2GTCandidate`.

### Current issue

Neither quantity reaches NanoAOD.

* **`L1gmtTkMuon`** inherited `hwIso = Var("hwIso()")` from `staMuTable`. That is the `L1Candidate` isolation *bit word*, and the Phase-2 GMT never fills it  `Isolation.h` leaves `mu.setHwIso(iso_)` commented out, under *"Disable isolation bit, sending isolation sumPT to GT"*. The branch is therefore identically zero, which is silent rather than obviously broken: measured over 27 TkMuons, `hwIso()` had exactly one distinct value, `0`.
* **`L1GTgmtTkMuon`** carries no isolation branch at all. `gtTkMuTable` clones `gtTkEleTable` but replaces `variables` wholesale, so the `hwIso`/`iso`/`relIso` entries defined for tkElectrons and tkPhotons are dropped, even though the producer does fill them for muons.

### Proposed change

Expose the sums the emulator actually computes, and make the two tables agree.

| branch | expression | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `L1gmtTkMuon.hwIsoSum` | `hwIsoSum()` | unsaturated sum, LSB 0.03125 GeV |
| `L1gmtTkMuon.hwIso` | `hwIsoSumAp()` | the 6-bit word sent to the GT, LSB 0.25 GeV |
| `L1gmtTkMuon.iso` | `phIso()` | absolute isolation [GeV] |
| `L1gmtTkMuon.relIso` | `phIso()/phPt()` | relative isolation |
| `L1GTgmtTkMuon.hwIso` | `hwIsolationPT_toInt()` | the same 6-bit word, as received by the GT |
| `L1GTgmtTkMuon.iso` | `isolationPT()` | absolute isolation [GeV] |
| `L1GTgmtTkMuon.relIso` | `isolationPT()/pt` | relative isolation |

The same `hwIso()` word is equally unfilled for the standalone muons, and `l1t::SAMuon` has no isolation of its own to put there, so the second commit removes `hwIso` from `staMuTable` altogether. That drops the constant-zero branch from `L1gmtMuon`, `L1gmtDispMuon` and the KMTF/OMTF/EMTF clones; over 50 PU events it had exactly one distinct value, `0`, across all 43 standalone muons. Because `gmtTkMuTable` clones `staMuTable.variables`, `hwIso` is then defined explicitly on the TkMuon table, where the quantity genuinely exists.

`hwIso` is defined from the GT word rather than left at zero, so that `L1gmtTkMuon.hwIso` and `L1GTgmtTkMuon.hwIso` hold the same quantity in the same units, consistent with the tkElectron and tkPhoton tables. Both table definitions carry a comment stating that this isolation is **track-based only**  a sum of L1 tracker track pT, with no calorimeter or PF/Puppi contribution  so it is not directly comparable with the Correlator Layer-2 isolation used for `tkEle`/`tkPho`.

A third commit then keeps that isolation off the **GT standalone muon** tables. `gtSaMuTable` and `gtSaDispMuTable` are clones of `gtTkMuTable`, so defining the three variables inside `gtTkMuTable`'s `variables` PSet propagated them to the standalone tables as well, where `L1GTProducer` sets no isolation at all -- not even `hwIsolationPT_` -- and all three accessors throw on an unset `Optional`:

```
Calling method for module SimpleP2GTCandidateFlatTableProducer/'gtSaMuTable'
Object doesn't have isolationPT
```

They are therefore defined after the two clones are taken, which is the pattern already used for `gtTkEleTable`'s extra variables. The `L1GTgmtTkMuon` branches are unchanged; `L1GTgmtMuon` and `L1GTgmtDispMuon` get no isolation, as before this series.

### Validation

50 events of `Phase2Fall26DIGI` `TT_TuneCP5_14TeV-powheg-pythia8_PU`, reading the stored `l1tTkMuonsGmt` and re-running `l1tGTProducer`:

```
TkMuons: 27 (GMT table), 27 (GT table)
non-zero hwIsoSum : 15 / 27   (max 2856 -> 89.250 GeV)
non-zero hwIso    : 15 / 27   (max 63 -> 15.75 GeV)

hwIso != min(hwIsoSum,511)>>3 : 0
iso   != 0.25 * hwIso         : 0
GT hwIso != GMT hwIso         : 0
```

So `hwIso` reproduces the `ap_ufixed<9, 9, AP_TRN, AP_SAT>` plus `>> 3` path exactly, `iso` is exactly `LSBGTiso * hwIso`, and the GMT and GT tables agree for every muon. The largest `hwIsoSum` seen, 2856 (89.25 GeV) against a saturated `hwIso` of 63 (15.75 GeV), is the case that motivates keeping the unsaturated sum alongside the GT word.

The same job on 50 events of no-PU `DYToLL_M-50` gives zero isolation for all 30 muons, with the three consistency checks still passing. That is the expected physics for isolated Z muons in an empty cone, not a regression  the PU sample is what exercises the variables.

The three commits were then exercised at production scale, in a `CMSSW_17_0_0_pre6` area carrying the same table definitions (with `isolationPT()` written as its python equivalent `hwIsolationPT_toInt() * 0.25`, the accessor not being in `17_0_X`), over Phase2Spring24 `TTTo2L2Nu_TuneCP5_14TeV` PU200. On 1000 events of the resulting NanoAOD, 3861 TkMuons:

```
non-zero iso                       :  432 / 3861  (11.2%)
L1gmtTkMuon.hwIso - L1GTgmtTkMuon.hwIso == 0 : 3861 / 3861  (100.00%, RMS 0.0000)
at the 6-bit ceiling (hwIso == 63) :  197 / 432   (45.6%)
  their hwIsoSum                   :  mean 42.3 GeV, max 171.0 GeV
L1GTgmtMuon / L1GTgmtDispMuon      :  no isolation branches
```

So the two tables agree muon-by-muon at scale, and the standalone GT tables are free of the branches that would have thrown. The 45.6% saturation fraction is the quantitative case for keeping the unsaturated `hwIsoSum` in the table.

### Discussion / questions

* Dropping `hwIso` from the standalone muon tables removes a branch that existing user code may read, even though it only ever contained zero. Flagging it as the one schema removal here, in case anyone would rather keep the branch for compatibility.
* `iso` uses `P2GTCandidate::isolationPT()`, which throws on an unset `Optional`. In any workflow where `l1tGTProducer` runs in the same job this is fine, but reading a file whose `P2GTCandidate`s predate the `isolationPT_` assignment does throw  encountered while preparing this. That is already true of the existing tkElectron and tkPhoton entries, so the behaviour is unchanged, and the alternative would be `hwIsolationPT_toInt() * 0.25`.
* Whether `relIso` is more useful built from the unsaturated `hwIsoSum` than from the saturated GT word is a matter of taste; the current choice keeps `iso` and `relIso` the same quantity. The production numbers above argue that it matters in practice: for 45.6% of isolated muons `iso` is clipped at 15.75 GeV while the true sum averages 42.3 GeV, so an analysis cutting on `relIso` as defined here silently treats every one of them alike. Happy to switch both `iso` and `relIso` to `hwIsoSum * 0.03125` if that is preferred -- it would, however, then no longer be the quantity the GT itself cuts on.

Feedback and alternative approaches are very welcome.
52426.title: [L1T] Phase2 L1Nano: fix TkMuon isolation branches, drop the unfilled hwIso from the SA muon tables

#### PR description:

cms-sw/cmssw#52372 introduced new Phase-2 L1 GT menus, with `v0p0_2026` as the new baseline. Every seed was renamed, so the Phase-2 HLT menu (`HLT_75e33`), which was written for `step1_2024`, no longer works with the new menu: 31 of its 33 L1-gated paths name seeds that `v0p0_2026` does not define.

This PR adds an opt-in customization, `customizeHLTforL1P2GTv0p0_2026` in `HLTrigger/Configuration/python/customizeHLTforCMSSW.py`, so the current HLT menu can run with `-s L1P2GT:v0p0_2026,HLT:75e33`:
- 17 seed names are mapped to their closest `v0p0_2026` seed. Each pair uses the same L1 objects with the same multiplicity, so only the thresholds change. Examples: `pSingleEGEle51`  `pSingleEGEle`, `pDoubleTkMuon15_7`  `pDoubleTkMu`, `pPuppiHT450`  `pHTSum`.
- `pIsoTkEleEGEle22_12` has no counterpart. It is dropped from the OR of `hltEGL1SeedsForDoubleEleIsolatedFilter`, which stays seeded by `pDoubleEGEle | pDoubleTkEle`.
- `pPuppiHT400_pQuadJet70_55_40_40` has no counterpart because `v0p0_2026` has no quad-jet algo. The quad-jet leg (`hltL1QuadJet70554040`) is removed, and the two HT + quad-jet + 3b paths fall back to `pHTSum` alone.

The customization is **not** called from `customizeHLTforCMSSW`, so the default `step1_2024` workflows are unchanged. A new addOnTest, `hlt_mc_Phase2_v0p0_2026`, runs `-s L1P2GT:v0p0_2026,HLT:75e33` with this customization applied.

The seed mapping is a draft, matched by object, multiplicity and cuts. It still needs confirmation from L1 DPG.

No changes are expected in the output of existing workflows.

#### PR validation:

- Applied the customization to all L1-gated `HLT_75e33` filters and checked that every L1 algo name they reference afterwards is defined in the `v0p0_2026` menu (57 algorithms).
- Checked that `hltL1QuadJet70554040` is removed from the seeding sequence.
- `addOnTests.py -t hlt_mc_Phase2_v0p0_2026`: <to be filled>

52448.author: mmusich
52448.body:
#### PR description:

The Run-3 HLT menus are generated from ConfDB, so their python files are consistent by construction and come with tooling (`getHLT.sh`, `hltListPaths`, `getEventContent.py`, `getDatasets.py`). The Phase-2 menu in `HLTrigger/Configuration/python/HLT_75e33` is maintained by hand, one `_cfi` per object, and has no equivalent tooling: nothing catches broken or stale imports, orphaned files, or modules whose configuration no longer matches the file name, and the HTML menu documentation is produced with scripts that live outside the release.

This PR adds two scripts to `HLTrigger/Configuration/scripts`:

- `hltPhase2MenuCheck`: static consistency checks of the `HLT_75e33` tree. Files are parsed with the python AST (nothing is executed, no `cmsenv` needed). Errors (exit code 1): syntax errors (E001), `fragment.load(...)` or imports of missing files (E002), symbols used but neither defined nor imported (E003). Warnings (fatal only with `--strict`): files not reached from any entry point (W101), imports from which nothing is used (W102), `X_cfi.py` not defining `X` (W103), symbols defined in several files (W104), files loaded twice (W105). Entry points are all files in `HLTrigger/Configuration/python` that reference `HLT_75e33` (e.g. `HLT_75e33_cff.py`, `HLT_NGTScouting_cff.py`); more can be given with `--root`. Findings can be written as JSON and selectively ignored with `--ignore`.
- `hltPhase2MenuDump`: loads a configuration containing the menu (e.g. from `cmsDriver.py -s L1P2GT,HLT:75e33 --no_exec`) and provides:
  - text listings: `--list paths|seeds|modules|datasets|eventcontent` (Phase-2 counterparts of `hltListPaths`, `getDatasets.py`, `getEventContent.py`);
  - a JSON model of the menu (`--json`), which can also be used as input;
  - a static, self-contained HTML site (`-o DIR`, no external assets or network access, light/dark mode): a searchable and sortable path table (L1 seed, number of modules and filters, last filter); one page per path with the ordered module chain (filters, Task members, negated/ignored modules), the selection parameters of each filter, and the products consumed by the path whose producers it does not schedule; one page per module (plugin type, link to the plugin source and to its `_cfi` file, paths using it, inputs, consumers, full python dump); EventSetup, services, outputs/datasets pages; a checks page (modules in no path, paths not in the schedule, paths without an L1 seed module);
  - `--compare OTHER.json`: a differences page between two menus (e.g. default vs `alpaka` vs `ticl_v5`): paths and modules added, removed, reordered or reconfigured, and changed L1 seeds.

It also adds a `README.md` in `HLTrigger/Configuration/python/HLT_75e33/test` documenting the tools.

No change in any workflow output is expected: the PR only adds scripts, tests and documentation.

The HTML dumper is meant to replace the out-of-release scripts currently used to produce the Phase-2 menu documentation pages (e.g. https://evernazz.web.cern.ch/evernazz/NGT/site/Phase2Menu/GettingStarted/).

#### PR validation:

- New unit tests in `HLTrigger/Configuration/test`:
  - `test_hltPhase2MenuCheck.py`: runs the checker on a synthetic `HLT_75e33` tree with one planted defect per rule and requires exactly the expected findings and exit code (external star imports, e.g. from `RecoTracker`, must not produce false E003);
  - `test_hltPhase2MenuTools.sh`: static checks of the real tree, `cmsDriver.py` (`--no_exec`) for the default and `alpaka` menus, JSON/HTML dumps, sanity checks of the menu model (minimum number of `HLT_` paths, no empty paths, no references to unknown modules) and the diff page. Conditions, geometry and era can be overridden with `P2_CONDITIONS`, `P2_GEOMETRY`, `P2_ERA`.
- Both are registered in `HLTrigger/Configuration/test/BuildFile.xml` (`testHLTPhase2MenuCheckSelfTest`, `testHLTPhase2MenuCheck`, `testHLTPhase2MenuTools`).
- `scram b runtests_testHLTPhase2MenuTools` and `scram b runtests_testHLTPhase2MenuCheck` in `CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-11-08-0000`.
- HTML output inspected for the default menu: [link to the generated page](https://marcomusich.web.cern.ch/display/html_default/)

52455.author: felicepantaleo
52455.body:
`ticl::assignPCAtoTracksters` (`RecoTICL/Common/src/TrackstersPCA.cc`) divides the covariance and the spreads by `1 - sum of squared weights`. This value is 0 when one layer cluster carries all the energy of the PCA set, for example when the cleaning keeps only one layer cluster. The covariance and the spreads are then NaN or inf.

With this PR, the function writes zeros in the PCA variables of such a trackster: a PCA set with fewer than 2 layer clusters, or a normalisation that is not positive. The output changes only for these tracksters.

#### PR validation:

- New unit test `testTrackstersPCA` (`RecoTICL/Common/test`): one layer cluster with all the energy gives a PCA of zeros, and three layer clusters along a line give a finite PCA with the principal axis along the line.
52455.title: TrackstersPCA: no NaN or inf when one layer cluster carries all the energy

52457.author: felicepantaleo
52457.body:
This PR changes TICL code that the default reconstruction and the TICLv6 interpretation (a follow-up PR) share. In the default reconstruction it changes the content of some tracksters, and no candidate.

- Merged trackster PID: a trackster made by merging (the four `Trackster::mergeTracksters` overloads) had all PID probabilities at 0. It now has the unknown probability at 1 (`setProbabilitiesUnknown`), so its probabilities are a distribution. No data member changes.
- `General` interpretation: when it links a merged trackster to a track, it sets the PID from zero, so the unknown probability of the merge does not remain next to the charged hadron or electron probability.
- PCA of small tracksters: one or two layer clusters give no principal axes. `assignPCAtoTracksters` now gives such a trackster a geometric frame: the main axis from the origin to the barycenter, the second axis azimuthal, the third their cross product. The widths are the size w of the seed cell, as the standard deviation w/sqrt(12): for silicon twice the distance to the cell side and the sensor thickness, for scintillator the tile (rT dEta by rT dPhi) and 0.3 cm. A cell that is not in the geometry gives zero widths.
- Superclustering DNN: one PID test for the seeds and for the single-trackster superclusters, and a new `emissionPIDThreshold` (default 0) for the single-trackster superclusters. With the defaults the superclusters do not change, and the configuration sets no value equal to a default. An emission threshold without the PID filter is a configuration error.
- `PFTICLProducer`: a TICL candidate with PDG id 111 becomes a PF photon. Before, it became a PF candidate of type X.
52457.title: TICL: PID of merged tracksters, PCA frame of small tracksters, superclustering emission threshold, pi0 in pfTICL
